headline: Elon Musk announces SpaceXAI will be rebranded to SpaceXSI following Trump's executive order on AI

sources.excerpt: “No more AI,” Musk said in a post early Sunday, saying the “super intelligence” moniker is “better.” In response to a user who asked whether Musk would rename his company to “SpaceXSI,” the billionaire said, “Yes, we will make that change.” “SpaceX is a super intelligence company,” he said in another post early Sunday. As of Sunday morning, the website and social media accounts for Musk’s company still say SpaceXAI, and he has not provided any additional details or timeline for an official name change. Last week, Trump signed an executive order directing federal departments and agencies to use “super intelligence” and “SI” in official communications. The executive branch will no longer “acknowledge the usage of ‘Artificial Intelligence’ and ‘AI’ in any applicable setting,” Trump’s executive order states. The order says “today’s frontier systems do much more than imitate or automate discrete aspects of human intelligence,” and that new technologies “far exceed what was envisioned when the term ‘Artificial Intelligence’ first came into use.” Trump suggested the idea of a name change on Truth Social last month, creating a poll asking users whether they would rather AI be rebranded to “supreme intelligence,” “extreme intelligence” or “superior intelligence.” In his post, Trump claimed “many people” think AI is an “inaccurate, and very ineloquent,” term. “Superior intelligence” won that poll with 41% of the vote, but Trump posted a new poll the following day removing “supreme intelligence,” claiming it was losing “probably because of its relationship to the Supreme Court.” “Superior intelligence” won the second poll with 52% of the vote. Again, Trump posted a new poll the following day pitting a new option — “super intelligence” — against “superior intelligence,” which “super intelligence” won decisively with 65% of the vote. Whether other leading AI companies will follow suit and adopt the “SI” branding remains unknown. Demand for website domains ending in “.si,” typically used for Slovenian domains, have surged since Trump’s announcement, the BBC reported. Registry SI spokesperson Klara Herman said 44,000 websites ending in “.si” were registered in September, a 2,199% increase from August. Trump met with billionaire AI leaders at the White House last week, including Musk, Meta’s Mark Zuckerberg, Amazon’s Jeff Bezos, Nvidia’s Jensen Huang, Anthropic’s Dario Amodei, Google’s Sundar Pichai and Palantir’s Alex Karp. There, Trump and AI leaders signed the “White House Accord on Super Intelligence,” an agreement setting voluntary guardrails for AI companies. Among the components are to monitor “cybersecurity, biosecurity, and chemical threats, and to ensure that its models do not hack or access technical systems in unintended ways,” as well as to establish internal and external reviews ensuring “all of the controls, monitoring, and detection are operating as intended.” Also on Sunday, Trump announced the formation of the “Super Intelligence Force,” which he said will be “tasked with coordinating the effort of the Federal Government to ensure that America continues to lead the World in Super Intelligence.” The force will be led by a handful of administration officials, including Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton, Federal Trade Commission chairman Andrew Ferguson, Under Secretary of Defense for Research and Engineering Emil Michael and Office of Personnel Management director Scott Kupor.

Elon Musk is going above and beyond President Trump's recent directives to rename artificial intelligence, or AI, as super intelligence, or SI, by expressing a willingness to change the name of SpaceX's AI-focused unit to SpaceXSI. Meanwhile, as the sheer scale of Terafab becomes apparent, Elon Musk has conceded that SpaceX and Tesla are talking with TSMC to explore a more synergistic approach on the mega project. As a refresher, President Trump officially changed artificial intelligence, or AI, to "super intelligence" or SI on September 22, and called on the U.S. government to adopt the new term. In line with the president's directives, Elon Musk has now expressed a willingness to rebrand SpaceXAI to SpaceXSI, while declaring that "SpaceX is a super intelligence company." Meanwhile, President Trump has just announced the Super Intelligence Force, or SIF, initiative, which would liaise between the federal government and the wider industry on SI.

SpaceX CEO Elon Musk is rebranding the company’s artificial intelligence, or AI, arm following President Donald Trump’s executive order last week calling for AI to be referred to as "Super Intelligence," or SI. SpaceXAI will be renamed SpaceXSI, Musk confirmed in a post on X while responding to an X user. "Yes, we will make that change," he said. "No more AI. SI, it’s better," he said in another post. Sunday’s rebranding move also reinforces Musk’s close relationship with the Trump administration, during which xAI’s Grok was contracted to power certain government work while Musk served as a special adviser to Trump in 2025. SpaceXAI itself was created only a few months ago in July, after SpaceX acquired xAI in a $1.25 trillion deal that consolidated the two companies. Renaming the division SpaceXSI marks its second major identity change. Before being acquired by SpaceX, xAI operated as an independent startup founded by Musk in 2023. The company later acquired X Corp., formerly known as Twitter, in March 2025.
